subject: Proposed rolling-bucket term swap + usage-protected ramp (next steps)
messages:
From: Alec Rivera <alec@orbitalapps.com>
To: Connor Obrien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@orbitalapps.com>
Date: Fri, 01 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal strategy: rollover buckets & ramp options

Connor —

Quick note from our side as we start the renewal cycle. We like the idea of moving to a co-term that gives us more flexibility as our usage spikes through Q4 next year. Two primary asks from Orbital: 1) a way to preserve unused committed capacity (rollover bucket) for short-term surges, and 2) a protected ramp for the first 6 months of a multi-year term so we don't immediately burn into overage.

Attached is a raw export of last 12 months usage for context (monthly token and embedding totals).

High-level questions:
- Can Redwood offer a 24–36 month commit with a 6-month protected ramp and rollover pool that can be used for spikes?
- How will auto-renew interact with the rollover pool (we may want opt-out 60 days prior)?
- Any pricing guidance for mixing reserved capacity + burst credits?

Procurement looped in (procure@orbitalapps.com) to flag any contract constraints early. We aim to get commercial terms nailed down by mid-May.

Thanks,

Alec Rivera
Head of Platform
Orbital Apps

Attachments: Orbital_usage_export.csv (csv)

From: Connor Obrien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Alec Rivera <alec@orbitalapps.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 02 May 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal strategy: rollover buckets & ramp options

Alec — thanks for the clarity and the export. Monica (CSM) and Ben (SE) are looped here — we sketched three viable structures for Orbital that address your asks. TL;DR: we can do a multi-year commit with a dedicated rollover pool and a 6-month "usage-protection" ramp with limited consumption guarantees. Pricing and legal mechanics vary by structure.

Option A — 36mo anchor + 6mo protected ramp
- 36-month core commit (monthly billing cadence)
- First 6 months: protected ramp: overages forgiven up to 20% of baseline for each month (converted to rollover credits if unused)
- Rollover bucket: one-time annual bucket equal to 10% of annual committed tokens that can be spent for burst traffic. Unused rollover expires at term anniversary.
- Auto-renew default with 60-day opt-out window.

Option B — 24mo with quarterly convertible credits
- Shorter core term, higher per-unit discount, quarterly convertible credits for burst
- Auto-renew opt-out 45 days.

Option C — 12mo stepping commit + guaranteed top-up
- Year 1 smaller commit + automatic front-loaded credits for predictable onboarding spikes.

Attached: RDWD_rolling_bucket_proposal.xlsx (spreadsheet) — includes model P&L and sample pricing bands.

Next steps I recommend:
1) Confirm preferred term length (24/36/12) and appetite for rollover pool.
2) Monica to capture expected monthly baseline for the protected ramp.
3) Ben to confirm technical constraints (KV cache priming, prefix caching eligibility for rollover usage).
4) Procurement to flag contract must-haves so we can align SOW and DocuSign flow.

If you want, we can propose a mutual action plan and a single redline-friendly amendment that covers the rollover mechanics + auto-renew opt-out language. Happy to set a 30-minute call next week.

—Connor
Connor Obrien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: RDWD_rolling_bucket_proposal.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Connor Obrien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Orbital Apps — pricing approval & amendment language

Team —

Recap of customer request (Orbital Apps / RDWD-8472): 36mo preferred, wants a 6mo protected ramp and a rollover bucket for spikes. Procurement will need an opt-out window on auto-renew and explicit expiration rules for rollover credits.

Ask: can pricing approve a 12.5% blended discount on a 36mo anchor if we include a single annual rollover pool (10% of committed tokens) and the 6mo protection (overages converted to rollover credits)? If not, what's the minimum margin-friendly counter? Also need legal language for:
- Rollover credit calculation (monthly unused portion -> annual bucket)
- Rollover expiry and non-transferability
- Auto-renew opt-out window (recommend 60 days)

Ben — can you confirm there are no serving-side constraints for using the rollover pool to burst across regions (we may need to limit to US region initially)?

Proposed internal timeline:
- Today: align commercial (Connor/Monica/Ben)
- Tue 05/05: draft amendment (legal) and pricing model
- Thu 05/07: present to customer for sign-off and DocuSign prep

Lauren — tagging you for pricing sign-off on the blended discount and any SLA credit allowance (customer is sensitive to latency for their critical features).

Thanks — Connor
